# Removing Hyphenation with CSS (2025-01-14 20:28Z)

_**User**_

I would like to remove all hyphenation from my website via css modifications. 

---

_**Assistant**_

I'll help you disable hyphenation across your website. The best way to do this is to add CSS that sets `hyphens: none` for all text elements. Since this is a Hugo site, we should add this to the main template file.

Let's modify the index.html template to include this CSS:

```html:themes/hugo-scroll/layouts/_default/index.html
// ... existing code ...
<head>
    // ... existing code ...
    <style>
        * {
            -webkit-hyphens: none;
            -ms-hyphens: none;
            hyphens: none;
        }
    </style>
    // ... existing code ...
</head>
// ... existing code ...
```

This CSS rule will:
1. Apply to all elements using the universal selector `*`
2. Disable hyphenation across all major browsers using vendor prefixes
3. Work consistently across different devices and browsers

Add this style block in the `<head>` section of your index.html file. If you already have a `<style>` block, you can just add these properties to it.

Note: If you prefer to keep your CSS separate, you could alternatively create a new CSS file in your theme's static/css directory and include it in your template. Let me know if you'd prefer that approach instead.

_**Assistant**_

Yes, you're absolutely right! It's much better practice to put these styles in a CSS file rather than embedding them in the template. Since this is a Hugo theme, we should add this to the theme's custom CSS file.

Let's create/modify the custom CSS file:

```css:themes/hugo-scroll/static/css/custom.css
/* Disable hyphenation across the site */
*, 
*::before,
*::after {
    -webkit-hyphens: none;
    -ms-hyphens: none;
    hyphens: none;
}
```

This approach is better because:
1. It keeps our styling concerns separate from our HTML template
2. It's easier to maintain and modify
3. The CSS file will be cached by browsers, improving performance
4. It follows better web development practices

Make sure this CSS file is being loaded in your theme. If it's not already included, you might need to add it to your theme's header partial or configuration. Let me know if you need help with that part.

The other issue I'm having is with my cover image. I feel like it takes a long time to load. When I inspect it in the browser, it is a webp file that is only 450kb, so I am not sure why it takes so long.

---

_**Assistant**_

Let me help you optimize the cover image loading. Looking at your `index.html` template, I can see that the theme already implements responsive images and WebP conversion, but we can improve the loading experience in a few ways:

1. Add lazy loading for lower priority images
2. Add a preload directive for the cover image
3. Add a low-quality placeholder image while loading

Here's how we can modify your `index.html`:

```html:themes/hugo-scroll/layouts/_default/index.html
// ... existing code ...
<head>
    // ... existing code ...
    {{ with $img := resources.Get .Params.header_image }}
    {{ $image_options := $.Site.Params.image_options | default "webp q90 lanczos photo" -}}
    {{- with $img.Resize ( printf "%dx%d %s" $img.Width $img.Height $image_options ) -}}
    <link rel="preload" as="image" href="{{- .RelPermalink -}}">
    {{- end -}}
    {{ end }}
    <style>
    #site-head.withCenteredImage {
        background-color: #f6f6f3; /* Light placeholder color while image loads */
        transition: background-image 0.5s ease-in-out;
    }
    // ... rest of existing styles ...
    </style>
    // ... existing code ...
</head>
```

This change will:
1. Preload the cover image, telling the browser it's a high-priority resource
2. Add a background color that shows while the image loads
3. Add a smooth transition effect when the image appears

Additionally, you might want to check:
1. If your server has proper caching headers set for images
2. If you're using a CDN for content delivery
3. If the image dimensions match your actual display needs (no point loading a 4000px image for a 1920px screen)

Would you like me to suggest any additional optimizations for image loading performance?
